structured_output.world_model:
W2 (empirical), after E040. Tip is E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. Fresh seeds 13-22 (E038) gave 0.7525, so the population mean is about 0.752 and the 0.75 bar has about 0.2 pp of headroom.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0.0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027). E034 stacked a freeze with +0.5 epoch and saved 0.40 s versus E027 at about 0 pp.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are in the tip. About 10 time-neutral boosters failed (E025, E029, E030, E032, wd, LS). Averaging, LR shape and wd sit at a flat optimum within about 0.2 pp. Anything that cuts training signal costs accuracy (E030, E032, E037, E039, E040).
3. Time tracks pixels. Early low resolution is nearly free up to 30% at 20 px (E026, E033). E040 pushed it to 40/0/30/30: it saved 0.12 s and cost 0.06 pp on seeds 0-2, which is inside noise but misses the 0.753 gate. The 28 and 32 px phases carry the accuracy (E018, E024).
4. Backward truncation on memory-bound large maps is the best lever (E028, E034, E036). E037 moved the freeze to 60%: it saved 0.25 s and cost 0.38 pp. E039 (BN folding) saved only about 0.03 s and lost 0.15 pp. The stem is nearly exhausted.
5. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any change to step count or RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about 0.2 pp. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: truncation savings were larger than modelled. Time-neutral accuracy gains were over-predicted. Accuracy fell whenever training signal was cut.

Unsure: whether bandwidth-bound levers transfer to the PCIe judge, and whether any further trim clears 0.753 on seeds 0-2. The tip is near the Pareto front, and any trim needs an accuracy refund paid in epochs.

forecasts.reason: Diagnostic with no recipe change; the arena is untouched, so the tip's numbers repeat.
Cutting 12 low-res steps saves about 0.1 s; accuracy is noise-dominated and likely just under the 0.753 gate.
An earlier freeze costs accuracy (E037) and only about half of group 1 is saved; likely a small loss.
Moving the freeze from 75% to 70% saves about 0.05 s with a small expected loss; hard to resolve at 3 seeds.
BN recalibration costs about 0.04 s; the gain is small if any, since the Lookahead BN mixture is probably fine.
16 px saves about 0.05 s for 35 steps and may cost a little accuracy; 1x1 maps are poor features.
Math-identical, so accuracy is bit-identical; saves about 0.03 s on trial 0 only, which is a 0.01 s mean.

cruxes: Does any further time trim keep the seeds 0-2 mean at or above 0.753, or is the tip already at the Pareto edge where every trim needs an epoch refund?
Is the 3-seed accuracy noise of about 0.2 pp from RNG re-rolls larger than the real effect of the remaining small levers?
Do the bandwidth-bound savings (freeze, whitening detach) transfer to the PCIe judge GPU?
